text:
hana-partnerships: Quick sync — OpenGrove sent a redistribution addendum for their 13B weights. They want us to list model in AWS/Azure marketplaces and allow bundling with our HW partner SKUs. They attached an addendum draft and asked for an embargoed joint announcement window. Can legal/ops/hw/product weigh in on blockers?
kevin-legal: Please drop the draft here. Quick flags: non-commercial/NC restrictions break marketplace commercial listings; attribution requirements can be OK but need clear customer-facing language; export controls + dual-use language to review.
samir-ops: Upload the addendum link pls and include the weights checksum, manifest, and provenance metadata so we can validate before ingest. Also we need the S3 path + KMS key policy if they're handing us encrypted artifacts.
hana-partnerships: Link: https://redwood.internal/drive/open-grove/addendum-draft-v1.pdf
kevin-legal: scanning now. Top suggested edits (high-level): 1) Replace any "non-commercial" clause with "commercially distributable" conditional on marketplace listing; 2) Add a redistribution addendum exhibit that maps allowed platforms and geo-restrictions; 3) Require signature of the addendum by partner and Redwood before marketplace publishing. Sample clause I recommend adding:
```
Redistribution Grant: Subject to the terms herein, Provider grants Distributor a non-exclusive, worldwide right to distribute Model Weights commercially via cloud marketplaces and hardware bundles. Distributor may sublicense customers for runtime inference. Any geo-restrictions or export-control limitations must be listed in Exhibit A.
```
jess-product: From a marketplace metadata POV we'll need: SKU id, short description (<=200 chars), tags (quantized/int8/13B), model-family, latency profile, and approved pricing tiers. Also we need an owner contact and a canonical README to include in the listing.
samir-ops: Ops checklist (short):
- verify SHA256(weight.tar.gz) matches provider manifest
- signed_manifest.json from provider with provenance fields (training-data-ack, license, commit hash)
- bucket ACL + KMS policy for the artifact
- scanning: malware/credential check on checkout
- pre-quantization test-run on our infra (sample prompts)
Can someone confirm who will get the manifest from provider?
hana-partnerships: I'll request the manifest + signed attestation today. Wanted to confirm: can we accept a CC-BY-SA style license? Kevin?
kevin-legal: CC-BY-SA is okay for redistribution as long as our marketplace terms don't conflict with share-alike obligations. For hardware bundles, share-alike can get messy — prefer a permissive addendum clause that grants distribution rights without imposing viral obligations on the bundle buyer. If provider insists on SA, we'll need an exception in the addendum for bundled distribution.
devon-hw: For bundling with ASIC vendor SKUs we need a one-liner for firmware/export restrictions. Also confirm whether marketplace listing needs a separate SKU for "bundle with Redwood-HW" vs "software-only". Prefer separate SKUs.
jess-product: Agreed — we should publish two SKUs:
```
OG13B-Redwood-SW-v1  # software-only, hourly inference pricing
OG13B-Redwood-HW-Bundle-v1  # includes certified hardware image + warranty mapping
```
Each SKU will need a distinct README and supported-region list.
kevin-legal: Also add an Exhibit A template for geo-blocking and export-control language. We'll include a clause: provider must disclose any LP export-control or sanctioned-country restrictions. If provider can't guarantee, we carve those countries out of the listing and add geo-blocking enforcement in the console.
samir-ops: Tech implementation note: geo-blocking for marketplace installs is doable via region-based routing + license check at provisioning time. We'll need a flag in the manifest: `allowed_regions: ["US","CA","EU"]`. Also require an entitlement token for bundle installs.
hana-partnerships: Timeline ask from provider: they'd like announcement week of May 11, embargo lift May 12 09:00 PT. Is that realistic?
jess-product: If we get signed addendum + artifacts by Apr 28, product + ops can complete listing and QA by May 8 — tight but doable. Need marketing to sign-off on messaging.
kevin-legal: Legal needs at least two business days after receiving the final addendum to sign. If they send v2 by Apr 26 we're okay.
devon-hw: HW image validation and supply-chain checks add ~5 business days. If we want bundles live May 12, we must lock firmware images and run hardware validation by May 5.
hana-partnerships: Action items: 1) Hana to request signed_manifest and checksum today (due Apr 21) 2) Kevin to produce addendum v2 with Exhibit A template (due Apr 26) 3) Samir to prepare ops checklist and entitlement flow (due Apr 30) 4) Jess to pre-draft SKU/readme templates (due Apr 28) 5) Devon to schedule HW validation window (start Apr 28)
kevin-legal: I'll drop addendum v2 to drive and ping for review. Quick draft term for attribution in customer-facing listing: "Model provided by OpenGrove; inference powered by Redwood Inference." That should be short and acceptable.
samir-ops: One more technical ask — require provider to sign the weights with an OpenPGP key and include key fingerprint in the manifest. That helps provenance checks during ingest.
jess-product: Good call. For marketplace copy we should prefer a neutral line: "Supports quantized and full-precision inference; see docs for latency and cost guidance."
hana-partnerships: I'll compile these notes and send a single email to the provider with a revised timeline and the addendum ask. Tagging @kevin-legal @samir-ops @devon-hw @jess-product for acknow.
kevin-legal: ack :thumbsup:
samir-ops: ack — will start a draft implementation ticket and share infra checklist link.
devon-hw: ack — booked validation window on infra calendar.
announce-bot: Scheduled: joint-announcement draft will be created once all signatures are present and all checks pass.
hana-partnerships: Thanks team — I'll update this thread when I have the signed_manifest and the provider's v2 addendum.
